quotes.text: Good afternoon. Today, the Board decided to leave the cash rate unchanged at 4.35 per cent.
Our forecasts are for inflation to ease through next year and be back around the midpoint of the target range by the end of 2027.
And before anyone asks, no, the Board did not discuss an interest rate cut at this meeting. It only discussed a raise and a stay.
And are we concerned? Yes, we’re concerned because the productive capacity of the economy is not growing, and you know this.
We think that it’s not a massive risk to financial stability.

summary.text: Responding to Jacob Shteyman’s question on further rate rises, Michele Bullock said the Board is not ruling out a need for further interest rate rises if inflation remains above target for much longer than forecast.

summary.text: Responding to Matt Cranston, Michele Bullock said the productive capacity of the economy is not growing and the economy cannot grow very fast without inflationary pressures.
